meta.tagline: A wooden bridge, a turquoise lake and a city in the mountains' box seat

pills: One of Europe's oldest wooden bridges
The lake of four cantons at the door
At the feet of Pilatus and Rigi

overview.title: Welcome to Lucerne
overview.intro: Lucerne is Switzerland's postcard face, and it manages it effortlessly: the flower-decked wooden Kapellbrücke stands over the turquoise Reuss, frescoed façades wrap the old squares, and behind them rises Pilatus's jagged silhouette. Steamers sail for the lake villages, cogwheel trains climb above the clouds — the city is small, but its stage is the entire Alps. Whoever hurries in Lucerne misses the real lesson of Swiss watchmaking: good things run on time, but they are lived slowly.

local_word.definition: The Swiss German greeting: entering a shop, meeting on a trail, on the steamer deck — it is said, and always returned. Saying 'Grüezi mitenand' (hello, everyone) to a group is the shortest way to a local's heart.

rules.title: Tie the mountain plan to the weather
rules.description: If Pilatus and Rigi are inside cloud, you'll see nothing up there but a white wall: the morning webcam check is step one of any Swiss mountain day. If it's overcast, make it a city-and-lake day — save the summit for a clear one.

rules.title: Count the steamer as sightseeing, not transport
rules.description: The lake boats are scheduled public transport, but every crossing is a mini cruise: included in the Swiss Travel Pass, and the first-class deck is the view's box seat. Even heading for a mountain railway, choose the route with the boat leg.

rules.title: Manage the price shock with the lunch menu
rules.description: Switzerland is expensive and Lucerne is no exception: strike the balance with weekday lunch menus (Tagesmenü), bakeries and supermarket terraces. Save the evening for one good restaurant — the remedy is simple; its application takes discipline.

quick_facts.label: Getting around
quick_facts.sub: The old town walks end to end

quick_facts.label: Signature
quick_facts.sub: The bridge dates from the 14th century

tip.label: The Lucerne philosophy
tip.text: In this city the plan has two layers: mountain if the sky is clear, lake and old town if it isn't. Learn to love both with the same flexibility and you'll leave Lucerne without losing a single day.

transport.title: Around Town and Lake
transport.intro: Lucerne stages a transport ballet: steamer, cogwheel train, cable car and railway dance in one ticketed system.

items.title: Arriving from Zurich
items.description: The direct train from Zurich airport reaches Lucerne station in an hour: the station sits right on the lakefront and the old town. Do the Swiss Travel Pass arithmetic instead of single tickets — boats and mountains get included.

items.title: The old town on foot
items.description: Everything between the Kapellbrücke, the squares and the Musegg wall sits in a quarter-hour circle: cobbles, frescoes and fountains — the walking is the sightseeing.

items.title: The lake steamers
items.description: Historic paddle steamers and modern boats serve the villages of the Vierwaldstättersee on a timetable: the Weggis, Vitznau and Flüelen line is the scenic classic. First class on deck buys box-seat pleasure for a small difference.

items.title: Mountain railways and cable cars
items.description: From Vitznau, Europe's first cogwheel railway climbs the Rigi; from Alpnachstad, the world's steepest cog line climbs Pilatus: both are engineering shows. The 'golden round trip' gathers boat + train + cable car into one loop.

items.title: The city buses
items.description: The bus network is practical for the Transport Museum and the lakeside quarters: tickets by app or machine. The guest card given to hotel visitors often makes city transport free — ask at reception.

callout.label: Golden round tip
callout.text: Do the Pilatus golden round clockwise: morning boat to Alpnachstad, the steepest cog railway to the summit, cable car down to Kriens. Time the boat leg for the sunny hours — the lake is half the tour.

stay.title: Where to Stay
stay.intro: In Lucerne the question is a view question: do you want to wake facing the bridge, the lake or the mountain?

local_word.definition: 'The Lake of the Four Forest Cantons': Lake Lucerne's real name and the founding geography of Switzerland. Each arm of the fjord-like lake faces a different canton — the name is long, the view longer.

items.name: Altstadt (the Old Town)
items.description: Among the frescoed squares and the bridges: walk to everything, with the morning bridge photo right outside. Quiet at night, flawless location — the classic for a first visit.

items.name: The lakefront — Nationalquai
items.description: Historic grand hotels along the quay with the lake-and-mountain panorama: Pilatus from the window, swans at breakfast. Prices scale with the view — for living the Swiss classic.

items.name: Around the station and Neustadt
items.description: The modern belt behind the station: zero distance to mountain and lake connections, prices a notch friendlier. The efficient base for early trains and late boats.

items.name: Tribschen and the south shore
items.description: The green peninsula side where Wagner's villa stands: lakeside walks, the lido beach and neighbourhood calm. Linked to the centre by bus or a pleasant shore walk.

items.name: Weggis and Vitznau
items.description: The lake riviera half an hour by boat: palm-lined quays, the foot of the Rigi and spa hotels. The choice that makes Lucerne your view instead of your base — with the mountain train at the door.

best_time.title: When to Go
best_time.intro: Lucerne is on stage in all four seasons: the lake in summer, snowy summits in winter, and in February one of Europe's loudest carnivals.

items.label: Spring
items.name: The Fresh Season
items.subtitle: Spring · Green slopes, calm quays
items.description: Snow shines on the summits while the lakeshore greens: the boat season opens fully, the terraces go up, and the crowds stay below summer levels. The airiest stretch of the mountain + lake balance.

callout.label: May tip
callout.text: In May go up the Rigi: spring below, snow views above — two seasons in one day. Deck sunshine on the boat home comes as a bonus.

items.label: Summer
items.name: Peak Lake Season
items.subtitle: Summer · Steamer decks, lido swims, the festival
items.description: The city at its fullest and brightest: lake swimming at the lido, evening quay concerts, and the classical music festival opening in mid-August. On the mountain railways, early morning is the rule.

callout.label: August note
callout.text: The midday queues on Pilatus and Rigi are serious: take the first boat + first train and live the summit before 11. Leave the afternoon to a lake swim and the old town.

items.label: Autumn
items.name: The Golden Lake
items.subtitle: Autumn · Seas of fog, copper forests
items.description: September is clear and calm; in October the slopes turn copper and the 'sea of fog' season begins — the city beneath the fog, the summits above the sun. This is the photographer's Lucerne.

callout.label: Fog tip
callout.text: If the city is wrapped in fog in October-November, don't mourn — rejoice: go up Rigi or Pilatus and sunny summits above a cloud sea await, with mountains like islands. Check the webcam; if the fog is thick and low, the day is yours.

items.label: Winter
items.name: Lights and Carnival
items.subtitle: Winter · Christmas market, snowy summits, Fasnacht
items.description: In December the old town lights up and the Christmas market opens; the summits offer skiing and sledging under snow. In February the city becomes unrecognisable: at Fasnacht, masked bands wake the town at 5 am.

callout.label: Fasnacht tip
callout.text: If you coincide with Fasnacht, forget sleeping: with the 'Urknall' blast at 5 am on Thursday, the squares surrender to masked bands. Be a participant, not a spectator — the confetti stays in your hair for days, and it's worth it.

eat.title: What to Eat
eat.intro: Lucerne's cooking is the lakeside form of the Swiss classics: buttery pastry, melted cheese and lake fish — with the chocolate finale mandatory.

local_word.definition: Lucerne's signature dish: a giant puff-pastry bowl filled with creamy veal-and-mushroom stew. The name means 'little ball pie' — it sits on the old town menus as the city's pride.

items.name: Lozärner Chügelipastete
items.description: Creamy stew beneath a crisp puff-pastry dome: the city's own invention and the Sunday-lunch classic. The portion is generous — arrive hungry.
items.tag: The city signature · in an old-town restaurant

items.name: Fondue and raclette
items.description: Melted cheese's two denominations: bread dipped in fondue, cheese scraped over potatoes for raclette. A winter classic, served all year for visitors — the white-wine escort is tradition.
items.tag: The cheese ritual · with white wine

items.name: Lake fish — Egli and felchen
items.description: The lake's perch (Egli) in butter, felchen from the grill: the local pride of the quay restaurants. White wine and a lake view alongside — here, simplicity is the luxury.
items.tag: Lake to table · on the quay

items.name: Älplermagronen — the herdsman's macaroni
items.description: Macaroni, potatoes, cream and mountain cheese in one pot, apple purée alongside: the filling classic of the Alpine huts. Its truest form is found in the mountain-station restaurants.

items.name: Bakery culture and the Willisauer Ringli
items.description: Fresh pretzels, buttery gipfeli and the region's rock-hard cinnamon ring, the Willisauer Ringli: bakery counters are the budget meal's address. Don't bite the Ringli — crack it, let it melt, be patient.

items.name: The chocolate finale
items.description: Praline counters and hot chocolate at the city's historic confectioners: the most legitimate form of a rainy-day plan. The supermarket shelf's Swiss chocolate balances the gift list — two different leagues, both real.
items.tag: Sweet close · from the praline counter

callout.label: Budget tip
callout.text: In Switzerland the lunch strategy is sacred: the Tagesmenü boards serve main + soup at half the evening price. The sunny-noon alternative classic: a supermarket lunch carried to a lakeside bench.

hidden_gems.title: Hidden Corners
hidden_gems.intro: Everyone sees the bridge; these six are Lucerne's backstage.

items.rarity: A clock lesson on the walls
items.name: The Musegg wall and towers
items.description: Several of the old wall's nine towers can be climbed: the Zyt tower's clock holds the privilege of striking one minute before all the city's clocks. From the walls, lake, city and mountains sit in one frame — entry free.

items.rarity: The saddest stone in the world
items.name: The Lion Monument's quiet hour
items.description: The wounded lion Mark Twain called 'the saddest stone in the world' lies carved into the rock face: at 8 am there is almost nobody before it. Go before the crowds — sorrow works in silence.

items.name: The Château Gütsch funicular
items.description: A mini funicular climbs to the fairytale castle hotel above the city: from the terrace, the lake and rooftops lie at your feet. The city's most graceful balcony for the price of a coffee.

items.name: The Wagner Museum at Tribschen
items.description: The lakeside villa where Wagner lived for years: he wrote the Siegfried Idyll here. Reached by the shore walk — museum + picnic lawn + lake swim fit the same half day.

items.name: The Bourbaki Panorama
items.description: A 112-metre circular painting from 1881 tells of the French army's refuge in Switzerland: the 'immersive experience' before cinema existed. The rainy day's most surprising plan.

items.name: The Lido and the Ufschötti lawns
items.description: The city beach Lido with its sand and the Ufschötti park with its lawn are lake swimming's two addresses: clear water, a Pilatus backdrop and Swiss-style quiet sunbathing. After 6 pm in summer is the locals' hour.

callout.label: Morning tip
callout.text: Walk the Kapellbrücke at 7 am: the flowers fresh, the bridge empty, Pilatus pink in first light. The same bridge becomes a selfie corridor by noon — print your postcard early, eat your croissant after.

traps.title: Tourist Traps
traps.intro: Lucerne is honest; its traps are the price tag and the cloud cover — both manageable.

items.name: A summit ticket on a cloudy day
items.description: Mountain tickets are expensive and the view from a cloud-bound summit is zero: whoever goes up 'since we're here' pays a fortune for a white wall.
items.instead: Check the webcam and forecast in the morning; if the cloud is low, do the opposite — climb above the fog sea. If the summit is fully socked in, trade the day for the lake-and-city programme: the ticket won't run away, the cloud will.

items.name: The watch-shop coach crowds
items.description: In the giant watch-and-souvenir stores where the tour buses unload, prices are negotiable and the atmosphere is baggage-carousel.
items.instead: If watches are your passion, enter the old town's boutique dealers; for souvenirs, step off Bahnhofstrasse. A store with a tour bus parked outside is the sign of one not meant for you.

items.name: Bridgehead menu prices
items.description: Some terraces with Kapellbrücke views add the view to the bill: an ordinary rösti at summit prices.
items.instead: Hunt the Tagesmenü boards two lanes in, or solve lunch with the bakery-supermarket classic. Save the view terrace for a single coffee — the bridge is the same bridge over coffee.

items.name: Skipping the pass arithmetic on mountain tickets
items.description: Buying Pilatus + Rigi + boats one by one drills a Swiss-sized hole in the wallet; yet the passes aren't automatically profitable for everyone either.
items.instead: Write out the route, total the single fares, compare against the Swiss Travel Pass / Half Fare Card. On a two-mountains-plus-boat plan the pass usually wins — on a single-mountain plan the sums change.

callout.label: Golden rule
callout.text: Two things in Lucerne never love haste: the mountain and the budget. Save the mountain for a clear sky and the big spend for a planned day — everything else in this city is within walking distance, and much of it free.

itinerary.title: Ready-Made Routes
itinerary.intro: If you hate planning, follow these flows. The times are flexible; keep the spirit, break the order.

plans.title: If You Have 1 Day
plans.subtitle: A postcard day from bridge to summit

steps.title: The Kapellbrücke morning
steps.description: Walk the bridge while it's empty and take the tower photo; a fresco round of the old squares + a bakery breakfast.

steps.title: The golden round's first leg
steps.description: Boat to Alpnachstad: lake, coffee and mountain silhouettes on deck. Then climb Pilatus on the world's steepest cog railway.

steps.title: The summit hour
steps.description: The Pilatus terraces and a short ridge walk: the lake's arms at your feet. Lunch of älplermagronen at the mountain restaurant.

steps.title: Cable car down + back to town
steps.description: Glide down to Kriens and bus back to the centre; stop at the Lion Monument — better in the afternoon lull.

steps.title: The Musegg wall
steps.description: Climb the towers and gather the lake-city-mountain panorama; a chocolate break in the old town on the way down.

steps.title: A quay evening
steps.description: A sunset walk on the Nationalquai, then a Chügelipastete or lake-fish dinner: a glass of white, Pilatus lighting up across the water.

plans.title: If You Have 3 Days
plans.subtitle: City, two mountains and the lake — the full Switzerland

steps.title: Classic Lucerne
steps.description: The one-day flow above: bridge, the Pilatus golden round, the walls, the quay.

steps.title: The Rigi and the lake riviera
steps.description: Boat to Vitznau and the historic cog railway up the Rigi: a summit walk + view terraces; a lake swim or spa pause at Weggis on the way down; the evening boat home — deck sunset included.

steps.title: Culture and farewell
steps.description: The Transport Museum (Switzerland's most entertaining museum) or Bourbaki + the Wagner villa in the morning; a Lido swim or the Gütsch funicular in the afternoon; a farewell dinner in the old town — closing over the fondue pot.

phrases.title: 5-Word Survival Kit
phrases.intro: Swiss German speaks its own melody; these five open smiles on the steamer and the summit alike.

items.meaning: Hello — 'Grüezi mitenand' for a group; the greeting of every hour
Thank you very much — French merci, folded Swiss-style
Enjoy your meal — said before eating, and to the neighbouring table too
Cheers! — eye contact is the rule in Switzerland too
Goodbye / see you — say it leaving a shop and they'll take you for a local
